sanskrit: paśya rādheya pāñcālān praṇunnān droṇasāyakaiḥ siṃheneva mṛgān vanyāṃs trāsitān dṛḍhadhanvanā
english: Behold, Rādheya, the Pāñcālas driven back by Droṇa's arrows, terrified by that mighty bowman as wild deer are terrified by a lion.

sanskrit: naite jātu punar yuddham īheyur iti me matiḥ yathā tu bhagnā droṇena vāteneva mahādrumāḥ
english: Never again, I think, will these men long for battle, broken as they are by Droṇa as great trees are broken by the wind.

sanskrit: ardyamānāḥ śarair ete rukmapuṅkhair mahātmanā pathā naikena gacchanti ghūrṇamānās tatas tataḥ
english: Tormented by the gold-feathered shafts of that great-souled one, they flee by no single road, reeling this way and that.

sanskrit: saṃniruddhāś ca kauravyair droṇena ca mahātmanā ete 'nye maṇḍalībhūtāḥ pāvakeneva kuñjarāḥ
english: Hemmed in by the Kauravas and by the great-souled Droṇa, these others have huddled into a ring, like elephants ringed about by fire.

sanskrit: bhramarair iva cāviṣṭā droṇasya niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ anyonyaṃ samalīyanta palāyanaparāyaṇāḥ
english: Beset as if by swarming bees by Droṇa's whetted arrows, bent wholly on flight, they cling close to one another.

sanskrit: eṣa bhīmo dṛḍhakrodho hīnaḥ pāṇḍavasṛñjayaiḥ madīyair āvṛto yodhaiḥ karṇa tarjayatīva mām
english: There stands Bhīma, fierce in his wrath, cut off from the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas, ringed about by my warriors, and yet, Karṇa, he seems to threaten me still.

sanskrit: vyaktaṃ droṇamayaṃ lokam adya paśyati durmatiḥ nirāśo jīvitān nūnam adya rājyāc ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Plainly that fool sees the whole world made of Droṇa today; surely now the Pāṇḍava has given up hope of life and of his kingdom.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca naiṣa jātu mahābāhur jīvann āhavam utsṛjet na cemān puruṣavyāghra siṃhanādān viśakṣyate
english: Karṇa said: Never, while he lives, will that mighty-armed one quit the fight, nor, O tiger among men, will he leave off these his lion-roars.

sanskrit: na cāpi pāṇḍavā yuddhe bhajyerann iti me matiḥ śūrāś ca balavantaś ca kṛtāstrā yuddhadurmadāḥ
english: Nor, I think, will the Pāṇḍavas be broken in battle, for they are brave and strong, masters of weapons, and frenzied for the fray.

sanskrit: viṣāgnidyūtasaṃkleśān vanavāsaṃ ca pāṇḍavāḥ smaramāṇā na hāsyanti saṃgrāmam iti me matiḥ
english: Remembering the poison, the fire, the gambling, and all their torments, and their exile in the forest, the Pāṇḍavas will not abandon the battle — so I judge.

sanskrit: nikṛto hi mahābāhur amitaujā vṛkodaraḥ varān varān hi kaunteyo rathodārān haniṣyati
english: Wronged as he has been, the mighty-armed Vṛkodara of measureless strength — that son of Kuntī — will slay our finest, the best of our great chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: asinā dhanuṣā śaktyā hayair nāgair narai rathaiḥ āyasena ca daṇḍena vrātān vrātān haniṣyati
english: With sword, with bow, with spear, with horses, elephants, men, and chariots, and with his iron mace, he will slay them in troop after troop.

sanskrit: tam ete cānuvartante sātyakipramukhā rathāḥ pāñcālāḥ kekayā matsyāḥ pāṇḍavāś ca viśeṣataḥ
english: And these chariot-warriors follow him, led by Sātyaki — the Pāñcālas, the Kekayas, the Matsyas, and above all the Pāṇḍavas themselves.

sanskrit: śūrāś ca balavantaś ca vikrāntāś ca mahārathāḥ viśeṣataś ca bhīmena saṃrabdhenābhicoditāḥ
english: Brave they are, and strong, and valiant — great chariot-warriors — and above all spurred on by the wrathful Bhīma.

sanskrit: te droṇam abhivartante sarvataḥ kurupuṃgavāḥ vṛkodaraṃ parīpsantaḥ sūryam abhragaṇā iva
english: From every side, those bulls among the Kurus close in upon Droṇa, seeking to shield Vṛkodara, as banks of cloud close round the sun.

sanskrit: ekāyanagatā hy ete pīḍayeyur yatavratam arakṣyamāṇaṃ śalabhā yathā dīpaṃ mumūrṣavaḥ asaṃśayaṃ kṛtāstrāś ca paryāptāś cāpi vāraṇe
english: Gathered into one single path, these men might press hard upon the steadfast keeper of vows, were he left unguarded — as moths bent on their own death press upon a lamp; for beyond doubt they are masters of weapons and fit to hold him off.

sanskrit: atibhāraṃ tv ahaṃ manye bhāradvāje samāhitam te śīghram anugacchāmo yatra droṇo vyavasthitaḥ kākā iva mahānāgaṃ mā vai hanyur yatavratam
english: Too heavy a burden, I think, has been laid upon the son of Bharadvāja; let us go swiftly to where Droṇa has taken his stand, lest, as crows would a great serpent, they slay the steadfast keeper of vows.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca rādheyasya vacaḥ śrutvā rājā duryodhanas tadā bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito rājan prāyād droṇarathaṃ prati
english: Saṃjaya said: Hearing the words of Rādheya, King Duryodhana then, together with his brothers, O king, set forth toward Droṇa's chariot.

sanskrit: tatrārāvo mahān āsīd ekaṃ droṇaṃ jighāṃsatām pāṇḍavānāṃ nivṛttānāṃ nānāvarṇair hayottamaiḥ
english: There arose a mighty uproar from the Pāṇḍavas, who had turned back with their splendid horses of many hues, all eager to kill Droṇa alone.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca sarveṣām eva me brūhi rathacihnāni saṃjaya ye droṇam abhyavartanta kruddhā bhīmapurogamāḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Tell me, Saṃjaya, the chariot-ensigns of every one of them — those who, with Bhīma at their head, in their fury bore down upon Droṇa.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca ṛśyavarṇair hayair dṛṣṭvā vyāyacchantaṃ vṛkodaram rajatāśvas tataḥ śūraḥ śaineyaḥ saṃnyavartata
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing Vṛkodara striving on with horses the color of the antelope, the brave Śaineya, his steeds silver-white, then turned to join him.

sanskrit: darśanīyās tu kāmbojāḥ śukapatraparicchadāḥ vahanto nakulaṃ śīghraṃ tāvakān abhidudruvuḥ
english: Bearing Nakula swiftly on, the comely Kāmboja horses, decked in trappings green as parrots' wings, rushed upon your men.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇās tu meghasaṃkāśāḥ sahadevam udāyudham bhīmavegā naravyāghram avahan vātaraṃhasaḥ
english: And dark horses like thunderclouds, terrible in their speed and swift as the wind, bore Sahadeva, that tiger among men, his weapon raised on high.

sanskrit: hemottamapraticchannair hayair vātasamair jave abhyavartanta sainyāni sarvāṇy eva yudhiṣṭhiram
english: With horses caparisoned in finest gold and matching the wind in speed, all the armies advanced about Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: rājñas tv anantaraṃ rājā pāñcālyo drupado 'bhavat jātarūpamayacchatraḥ sarvaiḥ svair abhirakṣitaḥ
english: Next to the king came the Pāñcāla king Drupada, beneath a parasol wrought of gold, guarded all about by his own men.

sanskrit: lalāmair haribhir yuktaiḥ sarvaśabdakṣamair yudhi rājñāṃ madhye maheṣvāsaḥ śāntabhīr abhyavartata
english: Drawn by handsome bay steeds, inured to every din of war, that mighty bowman, fearless and unmoved, advanced amid the kings.

sanskrit: taṃ virāṭo 'nvayāt paścāt saha śūrair mahārathaiḥ kekayāś ca śikhaṇḍī ca dhṛṣṭaketus tathaiva ca svaiḥ svaiḥ sainyaiḥ parivṛtā matsyarājānam anvayuḥ
english: Behind him followed Virāṭa with his brave great chariot-warriors; and the Kekayas, and Śikhaṇḍin, and Dhṛṣṭaketu likewise, each ringed by his own troops, followed the king of the Matsyas.

sanskrit: te tu pāṭalapuṣpāṇāṃ samavarṇā hayottamāḥ vahamānā vyarājanta matsyasyāmitraghātinaḥ
english: Excellent horses the color of trumpet-flowers, bearing on the foe-slaying king of the Matsyas, shone resplendent.

sanskrit: hāridrasamavarṇās tu javanā hemamālinaḥ putraṃ virāṭarājasya satvarāḥ samudāvahan
english: Swift horses turmeric-yellow in hue, garlanded with gold, bore in haste the son of King Virāṭa.

sanskrit: indragopakavarṇais tu bhrātaraḥ pañca kekayāḥ jātarūpasamābhāsaḥ sarve lohitakadhvajāḥ
english: Borne by horses red as the cochineal insect came the five Kekaya brothers, gleaming like gold, every one of them under a crimson banner.

sanskrit: te hemamālinaḥ śūrāḥ sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ varṣanta iva jīmūtāḥ pratyadṛśyanta daṃśitāḥ
english: Those heroes, garlanded in gold, all skilled in war and clad in armor, appeared like raining storm-clouds.

sanskrit: āmapātranibhākārāḥ pāñcālyam amitaujasam dāntās tāmrāruṇā yuktāḥ śikhaṇḍinam udāvahan
english: Well-broken horses, copper-red and the color of unbaked clay, yoked to his car, bore the Pāñcāla Śikhaṇḍin of boundless might.

sanskrit: tathā dvādaśasāhasrāḥ pāñcālānāṃ mahārathāḥ teṣāṃ tu ṣaṭ sahasrāṇi ye śikhaṇḍinam anvayuḥ
english: Twelve thousand were the great chariot-warriors of the Pāñcālas, and of these six thousand followed Śikhaṇḍin.

sanskrit: putraṃ tu śiśupālasya narasiṃhasya māriṣa ākrīḍanto vahanti sma sāraṅgaśabalā hayāḥ
english: And the son of Śiśupāla, that lion among men, O sire, was borne along by dappled, fawn-colored horses that seemed to sport as they ran.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭaketuś ca cedīnām ṛṣabho 'tibaloditaḥ kāmbojaiḥ śabalair aśvair abhyavartata durjayaḥ
english: And Dhṛṣṭaketu, that bull among the Cedis, swollen with surpassing might and hard to conquer, advanced with dappled Kāmboja steeds.

sanskrit: bṛhatkṣatraṃ tu kaikeyaṃ sukumāraṃ hayottamāḥ palāladhūmavarṇābhāḥ saindhavāḥ śīghram āvahan
english: And the delicate Bṛhatkṣatra of the Kaikeyas was borne swiftly on by excellent Saindhava horses the color of straw-smoke.

sanskrit: mallikākṣāḥ padmavarṇā bāhlijātāḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ śūraṃ śikhaṇḍinaḥ putraṃ kṣatradevam udāvahan
english: Bāhlika-bred horses, jasmine-eyed and lotus-hued, finely adorned, bore the brave Kṣatradeva, son of Śikhaṇḍin.

sanskrit: yuvānam avahan yuddhe krauñcavarṇā hayottamāḥ kāśyasyābhibhuvaḥ putraṃ sukumāraṃ mahāratham
english: Excellent horses the color of the curlew bore into battle the youthful Sukumāra, that great chariot-warrior, son of Abhibhū the king of Kāśi.

sanskrit: śvetās tu prativindhyaṃ taṃ kṛṣṇagrīvā manojavāḥ yantuḥ preṣyakarā rājan rājaputram udāvahan
english: White horses with black manes, swift as thought and obedient to the charioteer's command, bore the prince Prativindhya, O king.

sanskrit: sutasomaṃ tu yaṃ dhaumyāt pārthaḥ putram ayācata māṣapuṣpasavarṇās tam avahan vājino raṇe
english: Sutasoma, the son whom Pārtha had begged of Dhaumya, was borne in the battle by steeds the color of the bean-flower.

sanskrit: sahasrasomapratimā babhūvuḥ; pure kurūṇām udayendunāmni tasmiñ jātaḥ somasaṃkrandamadhye; yasmāt tasmāt sutasomo 'bhavat saḥ
english: Bright as a thousand moons they shone; and because he was born in that city of the Kurus called Udayendu, amid the rite of pressing the Soma, therefore he became known as Sutasoma.

sanskrit: nākuliṃ tu śatānīkaṃ śālapuṣpanibhā hayāḥ ādityataruṇaprakhyāḥ ślāghanīyam udāvahan
english: Horses like the blossoms of the sāla tree, radiant as the young rising sun, bore the praiseworthy Śatānīka, son of Nakula.

sanskrit: kāñcanapratimair yoktrair mayūragrīvasaṃnibhāḥ draupadeyaṃ naravyāghraṃ śrutakarmāṇam āvahan
english: Horses with the sheen of a peacock's neck, harnessed with traces of gold, bore Śrutakarman, son of Draupadī, that tiger among men.

sanskrit: śrutakīrtiṃ śrutanidhiṃ draupadeyaṃ hayottamāḥ ūhuḥ pārthasamaṃ yuddhe cāṣapatranibhā hayāḥ
english: Excellent horses the color of the blue jay's wing bore Śrutakīrti, that treasure of renown, son of Draupadī, the peer of Pārtha in battle.

sanskrit: yam āhur adhyardhaguṇaṃ kṛṣṇāt pārthāc ca saṃyuge abhimanyuṃ piśaṅgās taṃ kumāram avahan raṇe
english: Tawny horses bore into the fray the boy Abhimanyu, of whom men said that in combat he was half again the worth of Kṛṣṇa and of Pārtha.

sanskrit: ekas tu dhārtarāṣṭrebhyaḥ pāṇḍavān yaḥ samāśritaḥ taṃ bṛhanto mahākāyā yuyutsum avahan raṇe
english: And Yuyutsu, who alone of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons had taken refuge with the Pāṇḍavas, was borne into battle by tall, great-bodied steeds.

sanskrit: palālakāṇḍavarṇās tu vārdhakṣemiṃ tarasvinam ūhuḥ sutumule yuddhe hayā hṛṣṭāḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ
english: Spirited horses, finely adorned and the color of straw-stalks, bore the swift Vārdhakṣemi in that most tumultuous battle.

sanskrit: kumāraṃ śitipādās tu rukmapatrair uraśchadaiḥ saucittim avahan yuddhe yantuḥ preṣyakarā hayāḥ
english: White-footed horses, their breastplates leaved with gold, obedient to the charioteer's command, bore the young Saucitti into battle.

sanskrit: rukmapṛṣṭhāvakīrṇās tu kauśeyasadṛśā hayāḥ suvarṇamālinaḥ kṣāntāḥ śreṇimantam udāvahan
english: Horses smooth as silk, their backs strewn with gold, garlanded in gold and gentle of temper, bore Śreṇimat.

sanskrit: rukmamālādharāḥ śūrā hemavarṇāḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ kāśirājaṃ hayaśreṣṭhāḥ ślāghanīyam udāvahan
english: Spirited horses of golden hue, finely adorned and wearing golden garlands, the finest of steeds, bore the praiseworthy king of Kāśi.

sanskrit: astrāṇāṃ ca dhanurvede brāhme vede ca pāragam taṃ satyadhṛtim āyāntam aruṇāḥ samudāvahan
english: Ruddy horses bore on the advancing Satyadhṛti, a master to the very end of weapons, of the science of the bow, and of the Vedic lore of Brahman.

sanskrit: yaḥ sa pāñcālasenānīr droṇam aṃśam akalpayat pārāvatasavarṇāśvā dhṛṣṭadyumnam udāvahan
english: Horses dove-gray in color bore Dhṛṣṭadyumna, that commander of the Pāñcāla host, who had marked out Droṇa as his appointed share.

sanskrit: tam anvayāt satyadhṛtiḥ saucittir yuddhadurmadaḥ śreṇimān vasudānaś ca putraḥ kāśyasya cābhibho
english: Him there followed Satyadhṛti, and Saucitti frenzied for the fight, and Śreṇimat, and Vasudāna, and the son of the king of Kāśi, O lord.

sanskrit: yuktaiḥ paramakāmbojair javanair hemamālibhiḥ bhīṣayanto dviṣatsainyaṃ yamavaiśravaṇopamāḥ
english: Drawn by swift, gold-garlanded steeds of the finest Kāmboja breed, they struck terror into the enemy host, peers of Yama and of Vaiśravaṇa.

sanskrit: prabhadrakās tu pāñcālāḥ ṣaṭ sahasrāṇy udāyudhāḥ nānāvarṇair hayaśreṣṭhair hemacitrarathadhvajāḥ
english: And the Prabhadraka Pāñcālas, six thousand strong with weapons raised, their chariots and banners bright with gold, came on with the finest horses of many hues.

sanskrit: śaravrātair vidhunvantaḥ śatrūn vitatakārmukāḥ samānamṛtyavo bhūtvā dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ samanvayuḥ
english: Their bows full-drawn, shaking the foe with showers of arrows, vowed to a common death, they followed Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: babhrukauśeyavarṇās tu suvarṇavaramālinaḥ ūhur aglānamanasaś cekitānaṃ hayottamāḥ
english: Excellent horses the tawny color of silk, hung with garlands of choice gold, bore the unwearied-hearted Cekitāna.

sanskrit: indrāyudhasavarṇais tu kuntibhojo hayottamaiḥ āyāt suvaśyaiḥ purujin mātulaḥ savyasācinaḥ
english: Mounted on excellent, well-trained horses the color of Indra's bow, came Purujit Kuntibhoja, the maternal uncle of Savyasācin.

sanskrit: antarikṣasavarṇās tu tārakācitritā iva rājānaṃ rocamānaṃ te hayāḥ saṃkhye samāvahan
english: Horses the color of the sky, as though spangled with stars, bore King Rocamāna into the battle.

sanskrit: karburāḥ śitipādās tu svarṇajālaparicchadāḥ jārāsaṃdhiṃ hayaśreṣṭhāḥ sahadevam udāvahan
english: Excellent dappled horses with white feet, draped in netting of gold, bore Sahadeva, the son of Jarāsaṃdha.

sanskrit: ye tu puṣkaranālasya samavarṇā hayottamāḥ jave śyenasamāś citrāḥ sudāmānam udāvahan
english: Excellent dappled horses the color of the lotus-stalk, swift as hawks in speed, bore Sudāman.

sanskrit: śaśalohitavarṇās tu pāṇḍurodgatarājayaḥ pāñcālyaṃ gopateḥ putraṃ siṃhasenam udāvahan
english: Horses red as the hare, marked with pale streaks rising along their flanks, bore the Pāñcāla Siṃhasena, son of Gopati.

sanskrit: pāñcālānāṃ naravyāghro yaḥ khyāto janamejayaḥ tasya sarṣapapuṣpāṇāṃ tulyavarṇā hayottamāḥ
english: And he who was renowned among the Pāñcālas as Janamejaya, that tiger among men, had excellent horses the color of mustard-blossoms.

sanskrit: māṣavarṇās tu javanā bṛhanto hemamālinaḥ dadhipṛṣṭhāś candramukhāḥ pāñcālyam avahan drutam
english: Swift, tall horses the color of beans, garlanded with gold, curd-white along the back and moon-faced, bore the Pāñcāla onward at speed.

sanskrit: śūrāś ca bhadrakāś caiva śarakāṇḍanibhā hayāḥ padmakiñjalkavarṇābhā daṇḍadhāram udāvahan
english: And the brave and goodly horses, hued like reed-stalks and gleaming like the lotus-filament, bore Daṇḍadhāra.

sanskrit: bibhrato hemamālāś ca cakravākodarā hayāḥ kosalādhipateḥ putraṃ sukṣatraṃ vājino 'vahan
english: Steeds wearing garlands of gold, their bellies ruddy as the cakravāka bird's, bore Sukṣatra, son of the lord of Kosala.

sanskrit: śabalās tu bṛhanto 'śvā dāntā jāmbūnadasrajaḥ yuddhe satyadhṛtiṃ kṣaimim avahan prāṃśavaḥ śubhāḥ
english: Dappled horses, tall and stately, well-broken and decked with garlands of pure gold, bore in battle Satyadhṛti, son of Kṣema.

sanskrit: ekavarṇena sarveṇa dhvajena kavacena ca aśvaiś ca dhanuṣā caiva śuklaiḥ śuklo nyavartata
english: Banner, armor, horses, and bow all of one single hue and all white, Śukla turned and came on, white himself.

sanskrit: samudrasenaputraṃ tu sāmudrā rudratejasam aśvāḥ śaśāṅkasadṛśāś candradevam udāvahan
english: Sea-bred horses, white as the hare-marked moon, bore Candradeva, son of Samudrasena, fierce in his splendor as Rudra.

sanskrit: nīlotpalasavarṇās tu tapanīyavibhūṣitāḥ śaibyaṃ citrarathaṃ yuddhe citramālyāvahan hayāḥ
english: Horses the color of the blue lotus, adorned with refined gold and bright with garlands, bore into battle Citraratha of the Śaibyas.

sanskrit: kalāyapuṣpavarṇās tu śvetalohitarājayaḥ rathasenaṃ hayaśreṣṭhāḥ samūhur yuddhadurmadam
english: Excellent horses the color of the pea-flower, streaked with white and red, bore Rathasena, frenzied for the fight.

sanskrit: yaṃ tu sarvamanuṣyebhyaḥ prāhuḥ śūrataraṃ nṛpam taṃ paṭaccarahantāraṃ śukavarṇāvahan hayāḥ
english: And the king whom men called braver than all other men, that slayer of the Paṭaccaras, was borne by parrot-green horses.

sanskrit: citrāyudhaṃ citramālyaṃ citravarmāyudhadhvajam ūhuḥ kiṃśukapuṣpāṇāṃ tulyavarṇā hayottamāḥ
english: Excellent horses the color of kiṃśuka-blossoms bore Citrāyudha — bright of garland, bright of armor, weapon, and banner.

sanskrit: ekavarṇena sarveṇa dhvajena kavacena ca dhanuṣā rathavāhaiś ca nīlair nīlo 'bhyavartata
english: Banner, armor, bow, and chariot-steeds all of one single hue and all blue, Nīla came on, blue himself.

sanskrit: nānārūpai ratnacitrair varūthadhvajakārmukaiḥ vājidhvajapatākābhiś citraiś citro 'bhyavartata
english: With car-guards, banners, and bows of varied form bright with gems, with motley horse-pennons and standards, Citra came on, dappled himself.

sanskrit: ye tu puṣkarapatrasya tulyavarṇā hayottamāḥ te rocamānasya sutaṃ hemavarṇam udāvahan
english: Excellent horses the color of the lotus-leaf bore the golden-hued son of Rocamāna.

sanskrit: yodhāś ca bhadrakārāś ca śaradaṇḍānudaṇḍajāḥ śvetāṇḍāḥ kukkuṭāṇḍābhā daṇḍaketum udāvahan
english: And warlike, well-formed horses, bred along the Śaradaṇḍā and the Anudaṇḍā, white-flanked and gleaming like hens' eggs, bore Daṇḍaketu.

sanskrit: āṭarūṣakapuṣpābhā hayāḥ pāṇḍyānuyāyinām avahan rathamukhyānām ayutāni caturdaśa
english: Horses gleaming like the blossoms of the āṭarūṣaka bore fourteen myriads of the foremost chariot-warriors who followed the Pāṇḍyas.

sanskrit: nānārūpeṇa varṇena nānākṛtimukhā hayāḥ rathacakradhvajaṃ vīraṃ ghaṭotkacam udāvahan
english: Horses of varied hue, their faces of strange and varied form, bore the hero Ghaṭotkaca, whose banner bore the device of a chariot-wheel.

sanskrit: suvarṇavarṇā dharmajñam anīkasthaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram rājaśreṣṭhaṃ hayaśreṣṭhāḥ sarvataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nvayuḥ varṇaiś coccāvacair divyaiḥ sadaśvānāṃ prabhadrakāḥ
english: Gold-colored, the finest of steeds bore Yudhiṣṭhira, knower of dharma, best of kings, as he stood amid his host; and on every side, behind him, came the Prabhadrakas with their noble horses of high and low celestial hues.
